To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

partially connected phase-shifting networks with active/passive phase-shifting components can be more energy efficient compared to digital precoding, while fully connected phase-shifting systems exhibit poor energy efficiency.
partially connected hybrid transceivers can be more energy efficient than digital precoders, and active and passive phase shifters can offer an energy-spectral tradeoff.

(i) partially-connected hybrid transceivers with active phase shifters and quantized precoders are more energy-efficient compared with digital transceivers; and (ii) fully-connected hybrid transcevers with active phase shiftes are not energy-efficient compared with fully-connected hybrid transcievers with passive phase shifters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of low-resolution precoder structures that can be applied in massive MIMO systems to improve the energy efficiency.
the energy efficiency of mmWave massive MIMO systems and the impact of quantized hybrid analog/digital precoders.
the energy efficiency of hybrid precoding in the context of mmWave MIMO systems, which is an emerging topic of research.

partially connected hybrid systems with passive phase shifters offer a good tradeoff between energy efficiency and spectral efficiency.
